Dear Editor,

Please consider our manuscript, *Fourteen years of expanding but unequal health insurance coverage among Kenyan women of reproductive age: a multi-wave analysis of Kenya Demographic and Health Surveys 2008, 2014, and 2022*, for publication as a Research Article.

Earlier Kenyan studies have characterised insurance coverage one cross-section at a time. Using harmonised data from three KDHS rounds (42,244 women aged 15-49), we track the full NHIF policy era as a single trajectory. Coverage grew from 7.0% (95% CI 5.5% to 8.4%) in 2008 to 18.1% in 2014 and 28.9% (95% CI 27.5% to 30.2%) in 2022 — a 3.45-fold adjusted increase after accounting for compositional change. Wealth-related inequality narrowed but remained severe: the concentration index fell from 0.5279 to 0.3349, while in 2022 53.9% of women in the richest quintile were insured against 6.0% in the poorest, and 71.1% of all women remained uninsured.

The analysis required resolving a structural discontinuity in the source data: `v481` is entirely missing from the KDHS 2022 individual recode, so the 2022 wave must be drawn from the person recode (`sh27`, `sh28a-c`, `sh28x`) rather than the individual recode used for 2008 and 2014. We document this harmonisation crosswalk explicitly, since it is a prerequisite for any multi-wave Kenyan insurance analysis using these rounds.

The trajectory matters for interpreting the Social Health Authority transition of 1 October 2024: it shows that rapid aggregate expansion under NHIF did not deliver equitable coverage, which sets the benchmark SHA must exceed. The manuscript is original, is not under consideration elsewhere, and uses authorised de-identified survey microdata. All authors have approved the submission and declare no competing interests.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Nichodemus Werre Amollo
